source.title: The Scholars' Line
source.summary: How the four madhabs drew the boundary between permissible credit sales and forbidden riba.
source.author: Islamic Economics
source.body_text: The Quran bans riba. But what exactly is riba? Is a markup on a deferred sale the same as charging interest on a loan? The Hanafi school allowed bay' bi-thaman ajil, selling goods on credit at a higher price, while drawing a sharp line against lending money for a return. The Hanbalis were stricter, suspecting any time-value premium of concealing riba. The Shafi'is focused on the six commodities mentioned in the hadith. And the Malikis developed the concept of sadd al-dhara'i, blocking the means to forbidden ends. This episode walks through the classical debates on where legitimate commerce ends and prohibited interest begins, showing how these 8th-century discussions still define Islamic banking today.
